# T003 — Frontend transaction and call characterization

## Summary
Both workspace suites are discovered by the root command; 35 offline tests pass against unchanged application code.

## Changes
- Added six `frontend/tests/transaction-utils.test.ts` tests against unchanged utility code: deterministic ID/time/random generation, form parsing and initial audit, immutable audit append and metadata, en-US spoken currency/fallbacks, literal display formatting and UTC dates, phone layout, status presentation, and duration boundaries.
- Added fourteen `frontend/tests/call-service.test.ts` tests against unchanged `CallService`: POST URL/headers/JSON, initiating and dialing audits, sparse backend status merging, incoming audit precedence, retry count/DTMF reset, all six terminal statuses, cached replay, subscription cleanup, HTTP error variants, and polling recovery. Fetch is always stubbed, interval and wall-clock time are fake, and no service is contacted.
- Reviewed retry request against the complete JSON contract, verified terminal polling leaves no scheduled timer, and verified failed initiation leaves no timer before a later subscription; a subscription itself starts polling even when a cached terminal state is replayed, so the failed-initiation test does not claim otherwise.
- Added a small isolated `frontend/vitest.config.ts` to avoid loading the production Spark/Azure Vite plugins during offline tests. Added the only frontend test dependency, pinned Vitest 3.2.4 (Node 22/24 compatible), via `npm install --save-dev --save-exact vitest@3.2.4 --workspace frontend`; npm generated the root lock. No existing locked package versions changed. The frontend test script pins `TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8`; the root `npm test` now requires successful backend **and** frontend suites, and Vitest fails on no test discovery.
- No application, ACS, or deployment code changed. Observed behavior worth preserving: successful call initiation records its connection ID in audit metadata but leaves `transaction.callConnectionId` undefined until a backend status provides one. Sparse backend records default merchant/currency/retry count/audit/DTMF; empty incoming audit keeps existing audit, whereas nonempty incoming audit replaces it. Formatting uses a non-breaking space in en-US Intl AED amounts; display currency instead uses `toFixed(2)` and no thousands separator.

## Decisions
- Keep Vitest isolated from production Vite plugins to make test startup independent of Spark/Azure integrations; preserve oddities as characterization rather than alter the application. Node 22/24 compatibility follows Vitest 3.2.4's locked `>=22.0.0` engine; Node 24 execution is reserved for T004.

## Validation
- Node v22.23.3, npm 10.9.9; from repository root with `CI=true TZ=UTC LANG=C.UTF-8`: `npm ci` passed; `npm run build --if-present` passed (three previously observed CSS warnings); `npm test` passed **35/35**, 0 failed, 0 skipped (backend 15/15 unchanged, frontend 20/20 new); `npm run lint --if-present` passed with the same five preexisting warnings and no errors.
- To rerun: `npm run test --workspace frontend` or `npm test` from root. No test exclusions, production services or product fixes. Node 24 validation remains T004.

## Follow-ups and risks
- T004 must confirm clean install and both suites under Node 24. Three existing CSS optimizer warnings, five existing lint warnings, and dependency advisories remain outside T003.
